title: PPT Slide Spec
description: One slide's semantic design with optional page purpose and content classification, without title, hierarchy, placement, or page number.

core.description: The main takeaway the audience should retain from this page, not its title or a list of layout instructions.

type.description: Representation of this element: text for prose, list for items, metric for a key figure, quote for a quotation, table for tabular values, chart for data, diagram for relationships, code for a code sample, or asset for visual media. comparison is a page content_type; choose chart, table or diagram for a comparison element.

intent.description: What this element should communicate: the relevant content, evidence or relationship and its purpose on the page. Describe the intended content in natural language without inventing missing facts.

items.description: One planned content element, pairing a representation type with its communication intent.

elements.description: Ordered content elements planned for this page. Supplying this list replaces it completely; [] clears it. Each element describes what to communicate and how to represent it, not HTML source.

layout.description: Natural-language suggestion for arranging this page's content and reading order, such as a chart on the left and explanation on the right; not a template identifier or CSS.

purpose.description: Optional purpose of this page in the narrative: cover presents the topic and identity; introduction introduces the topic, background, problem, goals or structure; transition switches chapters or topics; content develops the body; conclusion closes with a summary, conclusions or action recommendations; other means a known purpose outside these categories. This is not a visual template. Omit when undetermined; never default to content or other. A saved content_type is allowed only when purpose is content.

content_type.description: Optional dominant communication mode of a body page: explanation explains concepts, definitions, principles or facts; comparison compares objects, differences and trade-offs; example illustrates through concrete cases or examples; guidance provides methods, steps or action recommendations; other means a known body-content mode outside these categories, such as an exercise or task. Allowed only when the saved purpose is content. Omit for mixed content or an undetermined mode; never default to other, and do not use other for unknown or insufficient information.
